servers.name: let me put you on about a github user named 347. so they wanted to fork an annisette server because sidestore's is god fucking awful and its server.json was down. so they host their own server.json to point at, but that didn't work. they blamed everything else that could be related before circling back to this, then hosting it on github pages... on the wrong site. so, they put it on a conveinently placed repo they made (which really isn't related) to point at their forked annisette server. this is where they are and they're praying that it works. however, it was SO close to. they logged in, but... no valid server found. odd, they LITERALLY JUST GAVE IT ONE!!!!! looking at the logs, they figured out that somehow, somewhere, it was using v1 instead of v3. what the fuck? anyways, with a little bit of (definetly not vibecoded) debugging, they realised that they got the fucking filename wrong like a dumbass. they try that and pray AGAIN that it works cause they starting to lose thier shit. now however, they blame the name for being this long, and set it to something short to, i don't know, "My Anisette" or some shit and forgets what the journey was. they join the discord server for shits and giggles and eventually they fix the issue itself. it wasn't anisette (suprisingly), it was the fucking VPN config. all along it was this iface bullshit that they had to get a port paste it bla bla type shit they would have NEVER guessed in months. but at least they got it working, right? well yeah duh. however they feel like something's missing... they don't know what, so they get LiveContainer from SideStore and her long lost twinulin LiveContainer2, then JIT, then help other people with SideStore even through injury, blood and weariness, and even make some friends on the way like IntelRyzen, WhosThatRetroGuy, pizzaman55, yotythepro, etc despite being very antisocial. Now you'd think the deep dark hole in their heart would be filled *now*, right? Nope. They remembered something. This name. So, they get the name of the anisette server and slap it on there, and even add what recently happnened. They're commiting this GitHub change to say, whoever knew, and whoever saw this monstrosity of an anisette server name, thank you for being there, even if all you saw was read fragments of it peiced together, lost to someone's poor memory. But that's the thing, noone did. Because all they saw was just a long ass anisette server name. Alright then. They decided to make it even MORE longer because, well, they're bored, and they have more to say. Their certs got revoked TWICE, so they had to reinstall, and somehow amidst all this series of events, they even start to learn from the environment around them (and may or may not have larped a little), and the helpers has started considering recruting them. However, this was the WORST time to consider, considering that school was starting in literally 1 and a half days, so they stepped back on the offer. Anyways, while I'm on the topic of bad news, their Fedora install got fucking nuked too, so now they're trying to debug that as well. damn nvram can't do anything for shit- anyways. Now they're back on their beefy 11-going-12 year old computer and tempoarly using that as their main computer, which still works suprisingly well. While we're on the topic of SideStore, they aren't really one to be an all-rounder about it. Sure, they know configurations and textbook stuff like iface, pairing files, and certs, but somehow what they just can't seem to get is names, shortcuts (which is suprisingly common with a lot of people in the SideStore server) and how to fix Health Check without going on fire. Sure, they can, but not easily. Most of the information they had to learn from people like astris and IntelRyzen (w intelryzen) or self-experience. Now they look back at their GitHub repo because they're bored and they found... /00. They should so swap this with /, what the hell are they doing? So, they're doing exactly that, renaming this from 00 to 3474nd0m.github.io and naming the old 3474nd0m.github.io to something like... idk, 1 or something. Hell yeah. Now that they've done that they look back at what they just did. why DID they do that? I don't know.
